Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 20, 11:57 AM ET. It had Tigers 41% and Wildcats 59%, projecting Tigers 1.7 – Wildcats 2.1 (3.9 total, Wildcats by 0.4).

Final: Tigers 3 – Wildcats 2. Wrong winner: it had Wildcats at 59%, and Tigers (41%) won.

Thin data: 0 of 6 key inputs were sourced (missing: JKST sets scored, JKST sets allowed, JKST lineup rating or past seasons, BCU sets scored, BCU sets allowed, BCU lineup rating or past seasons), so league averages filled the gaps. It was logged as a no-data call: graded and learned from, never offered as a bet.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Tigers came in with a 3% above average attack and a 4% leakier than average defense (no scoring on file: rated at the league average), worth about 10 and 10 games of evidence. Projected to score 1.7, they scored 3 (+1.3 sets, 73% over); projected to allow 2.1, they allowed 2 (−0.1 sets, 6% under).

Wildcats came in with a 4% above average attack and a 2% stingier than average defense (no scoring on file: rated at the league average), worth about 10 and 10 games of evidence. Projected to score 2.1, they scored 2 (−0.1 sets, 6% under); projected to allow 1.7, they allowed 3 (+1.3 sets, 73% over).

The bigger miss was Tigers' scoring (+1.3 sets against projection).

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 5 against 3.9 projected (+1.1), about the 92nd percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±0.8).

Margin: Tigers by 1 against Wildcats by 0.4 projected, about the 19th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±1.6).

An unusual result, but one the simulations saw regularly (roughly one game in six to one in twenty).

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

review.title: Against the market
review.body: No line was priced for this game (no posted odds, or not enough data to price one).

review.title: What could have made it wrong
review.body:
Flagged going in: inputs were missing (JKST sets scored, JKST sets allowed, JKST lineup rating or past seasons, BCU sets scored, BCU sets allowed, BCU lineup rating or past seasons); there were no odds to check the projection against.

The result was off its normal range without being an outlier, so the flags may have played a part.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×1.216 of the raw projection. It counts toward Volleyball scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections (it's how teams with no standings on the routes build a record of their own).

Across 559 graded Volleyball games the algo now scales scoring ×0.962 and gives home teams +0.2 sets. Team corrections so far: Tigers attack ×0.996, defense ×1.040 (4 games); Wildcats attack ×1.040, defense ×0.961 (4 games).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Wrong side, total outside its normal range, margin within its normal range, no bet.
